issue: Is the lifetime federal felon-in-possession ban in 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1) constitutional under the Second Amendment, given that it disarms felons permanently without an individualized inquiry into dangerousness, and do pre-Bruen precedents upholding it remain good law?

sides.position: Pre-Bruen precedents upholding § 922(g)(1) remain good law, and lifetime felon disarmament is constitutional without an individualized dangerousness inquiry.
cases: United States v. Dubois, 139 F.4th 887 (11th Cir. 2025)

sides.position: Bruen displaces the pre-Bruen framework, and lifetime felon disarmament is constitutionally suspect absent an individualized inquiry into whether the felon is dangerous.
cases: Range v. Att'y Gen., 124 F.4th 218 (3d Cir. 2024) (en banc)
United States v. Williams, 113 F.4th 637 (6th Cir. 2024)

quote: Our sister circuits are deeply divided on whether pre-Bruen precedents upholding section 922(g)(1) remain good law and on whether lifetime felon disarmament is constitutional absent some individualized inquiry into whether the individual felon is dangerous.
cite: United States v. Garrick Richardson, No. 24-3151 (D.C. Cir. 2026)
